api_assessment.assessment: Two ordered early stages require an explicit False before fallback; None blocks selection. Stage-three available alternatives are retained, unknown alternatives keep status UNKNOWN, different token strings remain CHOICE_UNRESOLVED, and equal token strings can share SELECTED. Availability accepts only exact bool/None. Event tokens are opaque identifiers; chronology, event truth and calendar conversion are not verified.

The strict bool/None domain rejects truthy substitutes. False dominates None in conjunction. The author-of-disease and disease-decreasing-and-leaving exceptions are negated while preserving unknown. SATISFIED means caller-supplied prerequisites match, not a prognosis or probability. The composite disease exception and other historical predicates remain caller-qualified.

Nonnegative exact ints/Fractions are interpreted as daily angular travel in arcseconds; equality at each threshold is false for that comparison. Booleans, floats and strings are rejected. This validates representation, not physical units: an integer supplied in degrees would still be interpreted as arcseconds. No ephemeris, actual retrogradation, aspect, or full illness rule is computed.

Degrees, minutes and seconds each accept exact int/Fraction or None; known components must lie in their individual half-open ranges, and the combined known position must lie below 30 degrees. Fractional components are added as supplied without rounding. Any missing component produces unknown remaining arc. time_unit is always None.

The namespace is exact and case-sensitive; key is converted with str, permitting integer house keys. The helper reads the selected JSON file and returns a detached deep copy. It does not verify a schema, source_only/clinical_mapping flags, a source hash, or the authenticity of a caller-selected path. The audit binds only the frozen default data.

Identities are enumerated before suite consumption. Distinct count is the size of a set; testsRun, failures, errors and skipped counts come from unittest, and exit status follows wasSuccessful. The runner writes logs/summary beside itself, so it was executed only in the private copy. Its retained summary hashes five input files after execution but does not record the runner hash or Python version; the candidate manifest and independent receipt supply those bindings for this review.
